description: Bare, blotched, hairless and shaped exactly like a person, coming at a walk with one hand open and green.
lore: Out on the warm black rock, exactly the shape of a person, bare and blotched and wearing nothing. What tells you at fifty paces is the arms: a walking person's arms swing, and these hang. It follows, and it does not hurry, and when it arrives it does not bite and does not claw. It reaches — one open hand, out and across, green standing in the seams of it, a gesture anybody would recognise. Everyone who has met one says the gesture is the worst part.

It kept things. A bronze locket grown in under the skin of its chest. A pitted silver ring on a finger it was never made for. Grave dirt in the creases. The ones who go through what a broken one leaves are not robbing it, they are reading it, and no name has ever been read off one.

[[characters/8c41be1e|Hearn]] went into [[lore/the_hole_under_the_mountain|the cave]] with the one organised attempt anyone ever made on it, and came out alone, and in all the years since has said exactly one thing about the inside: it asked politely. Last winter at [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]]'s fire, a cracker fresh off the black rock was describing the open hand. Hearn stood up, and asked which hand, and went out. He has not added anything since.
gm_notes: 'Which hand' is a leaf-level chill, not a beat: it confirms only that Hearn met something with hands in there, which B7 (hinted) already tolerates. Never let Hearn say a second sentence about the inside. The green's price and mechanics live in the stone record; keep them to one clause here.
